current_assessment.assessment: Q.14 a.6 rejects a generic common input as sufficient for proper knowledge where distinguishing conditions come from elsewhere. The positive q.14–15 proposal places many understood objects and imitability relations in one actual understanding through one essence; it already presupposes source cognition. A noncognitive generative constitution must likewise account for the differentiating conditions at the same universal scope. That common requirement does not identify productive containment with intentional presence, and neither is actual practical governance by itself. The proposed many-form objection supplies no exclusive first-source cognition conclusion. The full witness-local bundle and identity/maximality inputs remain required; no God-existence witness or source-governance conclusion follows from this continuation.
